summary: Shubhangni Gupta works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She was a PhD candidate at Stanford University in 2019, where she studied as a doctoral student (attested 2026).

Shuddhatam Prakash Jain is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at institutions including Central Sanskrit University and University of Rajasthan, later teaching at Central Sanskrit University, Mangalayatan University, Ghanaram Hariram College, and Somaiya Vidyavihar University.

Shudo Ishii (b. 1943) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University under Shigeo Kamata. He spent his career at Komazawa University, serving as lecturer, associate professor, and professor from 1984, and later held a post at Matsugaoka Bunko.

Shuhong Chang (1904–1994) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. After studying in China and France, he taught at Zhejiang University and the Central Academy of Fine Arts, and long served as director and honorary director of the Dunhuang Academy.

Shuichi Kato (1919–2008) was a scholar of Japanology, history, and philosophy who earned an MD from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of British Columbia, Sophia University, Ritsumeikan University, and the Kyoto Museum for World Peace.
Shuichi Maida (1906–1967) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and under Haya Akegarasu.

Shuichi Nara (b. 1961) works in Indology and philosophy. Educated at Keio University, he has served as a researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and lecturer at Chuo University (attested 2026).

Shuji Takayama is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held research and teaching positions attested at Ryukoku University and Bukkyo University (2003), as well as Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College and Musashino University (2006).

Shujiro Shimada (1907–1994) was a scholar of Japanology, sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1928 to 1931 and served on the faculty at Princeton University from circa 1964 to 1975.

Shujun Motegi (b. 1951) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He earned degrees from Banaras Hindu University, studying under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi, and Kyoto University, later serving as professor of ethics at Shinshu University.

Shuken Ito (b. 1947) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at Komazawa University. He spent his academic career at Komazawa University, rising to professor in 1991, and was a visiting professor at Aichi Gakuin University.
Shuman Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned a PhD from Northwestern University under Brook Ziporyn and also studied under traditional teacher Weijue Shi.

Shuming Liang (1893–1988) was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Shuntian Middle School, he joined the philosophy department at Peking University in 1917 and founded the Shandong Rural Reconstruction Institute and China Democratic League.

Shumpei Ueyama (1921–2012) was a scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and history. Educated at Kyoto University, he became a professor there, later serving as president of Kyoto City University of Arts and director of the Kyoto National Museum.
Shun Hidaka is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He served as a researcher at the Buddhist Art Resource Center in 2012 and as a lecturer at Otani University (attested 2014).

Shun'ei Hirai (b. 1930) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo, subsequently serving as professor and vice president at Komazawa University, where he became professor emeritus in 2001.
Shun'ei Mori is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. He held posts at Ryukoku University (attested 1990) and Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College (attested 1995).
Shunei Tsuboi (1923–2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Bukkyo University (attested 1963 and 1972).

Shunji Hosaka (b. 1956) is a religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University. He taught at Reitaku University, Chuo University, the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Shunkyo Katsumata (1909–1994) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Toyo University and Taisho University, where he served from around 1948 to 1983 and became emeritus professor.
